scope.intended_use: Machine-readable device-group, membership, policy-assignment, automation, user-targeting, and additive-permission guidance for an operator or automation client before binding a concept to a target-instance OpenAPI operation.
not_authoritative_for: Exact API methods, paths, parameters, schemas, filter operators, or responses
Target release activation or migration state
Current membership, assignment, action, or permission state
External-directory source-of-truth behavior not proven on the target

completeness.coverage_basis: First-party Relution device-group, user-based policy, device-group action, and permission documentation available on 2026-07-18, organized into eight stable operational concepts.
known_exclusions: Release-specific filter field and operator schemas
Customer-defined group filters, actions, schedules, and permission sets
Education-class behavior beyond user/security group scope
completeness.contract_boundary: Every method, path, identifier, filter schema, action payload, schedule representation, and permission wire value remains unresolved until the OpenAPI JSON exported from the exact target instance is supplied.

records.name: Device group model
records.summary: A Relution device group links devices with policies either manually as a static group or automatically from device properties as a dynamic group; groups are platform-independent even though policies and actions may be platform-specific.
capabilities: Create a named device group with an optional description
Choose Static or Dynamic as the group type
Link devices and policies through the group model
Use group membership as a policy-distribution audience
Attach event-based or scheduled actions where supported
Keep platform-independent membership distinct from platform-specific policy and action applicability
prerequisites: Confirm device-group functionality is active on the target release
Resolve organization and group type
Inventory all attached policies, actions, schedules, and downstream group references
Define expected membership and platform mix

scope.organization_behavior: Device groups are administered within an organization and can affect every current and future device member through attached policies and actions.

reasons: Membership changes can activate or remove policies
Group actions can run immediately or repeatedly
Platform-independent groups may contain devices that cannot apply every linked policy or action
risk.blast_radius: One explicitly changed member or every current and future member of the selected group.

required_for: Group creation, duplication, type or filter changes, activation, or deletion
Membership changes when policies or actions are attached
Policy, event-action, or schedule attachment

effects: Create, update, duplicate, activate, or delete a device group
Change membership, filters, policy links, actions, and schedules
external_effects: Can deliver or remove device configuration and trigger device or webhook actions
destructive_effects: Attached actions can delete, wipe, lock, reset, or otherwise disrupt devices
Removing critical policies can break management connectivity
concurrency_cautions: Re-read membership and all attachments immediately before mutation
Do not treat group creation as isolated when copied policies or actions are included
Evaluate platform applicability per member

preconditions: Resolve group ID, type, organization, active state, membership, filters, policies, actions, schedules, and dependencies
Freeze expected member set
read_back: Read direct group state, computed or manual membership, attached policies, actions, and schedules independently
audit: Match group, membership, policy-link, action, and schedule events to the actor and organization
functional_checks: Verify one approved pilot device receives only the intended compatible effects
stop_conditions: Membership changes outside the expected set
An attached effect was not analyzed
A device loses baseline connectivity or management

requirements: Capture group definition, membership or filter tree, attachments, dependencies, and active state
Preserve a known-good connectivity policy
Prepare action-specific compensation
limitations: Executed actions and removed device data may be irreversible
Dynamic membership may change again after restoration

contract_checks: Locate group definition, membership, filter, policy, action, and schedule operations separately
Confirm organization scope and immutable group-type behavior
Inspect duplicate and activation semantics for the target release

evidence.claim: Relution documents device groups as links between devices and policies, with Static and Dynamic group types and manual or property-based membership.
Relution documents that device groups are platform-independent and can trigger policies, actions, and scheduled jobs.

records.name: Static device group membership
records.summary: A static device group has manually managed device membership and manually linked policies; only policies that were already published can be linked.
capabilities: Add or remove individual devices manually
Link or unlink previously published policies manually
Bulk-add or bulk-remove selected devices from an existing static group in supported releases
Expose newly added devices to every associated policy
Preserve membership until an administrator changes it
prerequisites: Resolve exact static group ID and organization
Confirm every policy link references a published policy
Freeze the selected device set
Review all policies, actions, and schedules attached to the group

scope.organization_behavior: Manual membership and policy links operate within one organization; every selected device inherits the group's compatible attached effects.

reasons: Adding a device can immediately expose it to every linked policy and action
Bulk membership changes can expand the blast radius
Unpublished policy links are invalid according to the documented model
risk.blast_radius: One device by default, or every explicitly selected device in an approved bulk membership operation.

required_for: Adding or removing a device when effects are attached
Any bulk membership change
Linking or unlinking a policy
Deleting the group

effects: Add or remove manual device membership
external_effects: Membership activates or removes attached policy and action effects on devices
destructive_effects: Removal can revoke critical policy configuration
Attached actions may have destructive effects
concurrency_cautions: Re-read group attachments and selected devices immediately before change
Do not infer that bulk membership is atomic or idempotent without the target contract
Inspect per-device results

preconditions: Group type is Static
Every selected device is identified by a stable ID
Every linked policy is published
Exact before membership is captured
read_back: Read the direct group membership and policy links after mutation
Read each affected device's group and policy status
audit: Match static membership and policy-link events for every affected object
functional_checks: Verify one approved added or removed pilot receives the intended policy delta
stop_conditions: An unexpected device or attached action is affected

requirements: Capture exact device IDs and policy links
Reverse only successful per-device changes after a partial bulk result
Retain critical baseline assignments
limitations: Policy removal or attached actions may already have changed device state
Device check-in is required for compensating policy delivery

contract_checks: Confirm the group is Static before locating membership mutations
Separate individual and bulk operations and inspect partial-result behavior
Verify policy publication preconditions

evidence.claim: Relution documents manual static-group device and policy links, requires linked policies to be previously published, and documents bulk add/remove for selected devices in release 26.1.

records.name: Dynamic device group filters and dependency safety
records.summary: A dynamic device group computes membership automatically in real time from a Boolean AND/OR filter tree; direct manual membership is not valid, and supported group-reference filters can include or exclude other static or dynamic groups.
capabilities: Compute membership in the background in real time
Combine filter predicates with ordinary logical AND and OR semantics
Target device properties, linked users, or user groups where supported
Include or exclude one or more existing static or dynamic device groups as filter conditions in supported releases
Preserve the complete nested Boolean filter tree rather than flattening it
Use one device serial as a pilot constraint before wider matching
prerequisites: Resolve exact dynamic group and organization
Represent the complete nested AND/OR expression
Enumerate every referenced group and build a directed dependency graph
Reject self-reference and dependency cycles
Compute and review expected pilot membership before attaching effects
Preserve a critical baseline Wi-Fi or management-connectivity path
sensitive_value_classes: Security and compliance attributes used as filters

scope.organization_behavior: The filter is evaluated inside the group's organization; changes can continuously add or remove matching devices and thereby activate or revoke attached effects.

reasons: A filter edit recalculates membership in real time
Mutually dependent group filters can produce endless loops
Revoking a baseline Wi-Fi policy can sever management connectivity
A broad OR branch or negation can match far more devices than intended
risk.blast_radius: Every device matching the Boolean expression now or after future inventory, user, compliance, or referenced-group changes.

required_for: Creating or changing a dynamic filter
Adding include or exclude group references
Attaching policies or actions
Activating a group after pilot evaluation

effects: Change the real-time computed membership by editing filter predicates, Boolean structure, or group references
external_effects: Membership transitions can apply or remove policies and trigger event actions
destructive_effects: A filter error can remove critical Wi-Fi or security configuration and can trigger destructive actions repeatedly
concurrency_cautions: Recompute expected membership from fresh inventory immediately before approval
Reject cycles of any length, not only direct mutual references
Detect filters or actions that change their own membership inputs

preconditions: Group type is Dynamic
Boolean tree and referenced-group graph are captured exactly
Dependency graph is acyclic
Expected pilot include/exclude set is frozen
Baseline connectivity is independent of the group
read_back: Read the exact saved Boolean filter tree and referenced groups
Read computed membership repeatedly across the agreed stabilization window
Read attached policy and action effects per pilot
audit: Match dynamic-filter, group-reference, membership, policy, and action events
functional_checks: Start with one serial-number-constrained pilot and test every AND/OR branch and exclusion before broadening
stop_conditions: A critical Wi-Fi or management baseline could be removed
An action mutates a reachable filter field

requirements: Capture the complete prior Boolean tree and referenced-group graph
Detach hazardous actions before broad filter recovery when separately authorized
Keep a static pilot and baseline connectivity group
limitations: Real-time membership may change again while inventory or referenced groups change
Actions already triggered by entry or exit may be irreversible

contract_checks: Inspect the recursive filter-expression schema without flattening it
Confirm supported fields, operators, null handling, negation, and grouping
Locate computed-membership preview/read operations and group-reference identifiers

evidence.claim: Relution documents real-time dynamic membership, no direct manual control, AND/OR Boolean filters, device-group include/exclude filters, pilot testing, Wi-Fi baseline hazards, mutually dependent groups, and endless-loop risk.
Safety recommendation: model referenced groups as a directed graph and reject self-links or dependency cycles of any length before mutation.

records.name: Device-group policy assignment
records.summary: Device groups are the default policy-assignment boundary: linked published policies become active for compatible member devices, while membership changes can add or remove those effective policies.
capabilities: Attach previously published policies to a device group
Apply compatible linked policies to current and future members
Remove policy reach when membership or a link is removed
Use static manual membership or dynamic computed membership as the audience
Observe policy assignment, delivery status, and functional outcome separately
prerequisites: Every selected policy is already published
Resolve group type, current membership, and expected future membership
Confirm platform compatibility for every policy-member pair
Review policy priority and per-device activation overrides
Review attached actions that may run on membership transitions

scope.organization_behavior: A group-policy link is organization-scoped; global policy visibility must still be resolved separately from assignment in the consuming organization.

reasons: A single link can affect the entire group and future members
Platform-independent groups may include incompatible devices
Removing a baseline policy can break connectivity
Dynamic membership can change after approval
risk.blast_radius: Every current and future compatible member of the selected group.

required_for: Linking or unlinking any policy
Changing membership or filters while policies are linked
Bulk policy assignment
Changing a critical baseline policy

effects: Attach or detach a published policy
Change membership that controls policy reach
external_effects: Delivers, updates, changes, or removes managed-device configuration
destructive_effects: Can remove network, certificate, security, application, or account configuration
concurrency_cautions: Freeze membership and policy versions at approval time
Re-read priority and per-device overrides
Track per-device convergence without unbounded retries

preconditions: Policy publication and platform are confirmed
Exact group and membership are resolved
Priority conflicts and critical baselines are reviewed
read_back: Read group-policy links, membership, published version, per-device activation state, and each pilot policy status
audit: Match policy-link, membership, publication, and per-device override events
functional_checks: Verify intended configuration on one compatible pilot per affected platform
stop_conditions: Status or behavior does not converge

requirements: Capture prior links, memberships, policy versions, priorities, and overrides
Preserve a separately assigned management-connectivity baseline
limitations: Removal does not instantly reverse device-side effects
Compensation depends on device check-in and may need a new policy publication

contract_checks: Bind group-policy link operations separately from publication and membership
Confirm organization and platform constraints
Locate per-device effective policy, version, activation, and status reads

evidence.claim: Relution documents device groups as the device-policy link and states that only previously published policies can be linked to static groups.
Relution documents that policies assigned to a dynamic device group activate as a matching user signs in and deactivate when that user signs out.

records.name: User-based policy targeting through dynamic device groups
records.summary: A dynamic device group can filter on an individual Relution user or user-group membership so that sign-in adds the user's device to the group and activates linked policies, while sign-out removes the device and deactivates those policies.
capabilities: Filter a dynamic device group by one individual user
Filter by membership in a Relution user group
Add a signed-in user's device to the matching dynamic group
Apply policies assigned to that device group while the user matches
Remove the device and deactivate those policies when the user signs out
Include all affected devices when the same user is signed in on multiple devices
prerequisites: Users exist in Relution
User-group membership exists when group targeting is used
Devices are enrolled and can be assigned to users
Administrator has sufficient organization permissions
Policies are published and attached to the dynamic device group
Shared-device and simultaneous-session behavior is understood
sensitive_value_classes: Private Exchange or other per-user configuration

scope.organization_behavior: Users, user groups, devices, and the dynamic device group must be resolved within the intended organization; all simultaneously signed-in devices may match.

reasons: User-group changes can alter policy targeting for many people
Sign-in and sign-out automatically activate and deactivate policy
Multiple devices can match one identity
Per-user mail, VPN, or relaxed-restriction payloads contain sensitive state
risk.blast_radius: One user's current devices or every device used by members of the selected user group.

required_for: Creating or changing user or user-group filters
Attaching policies
Changing source user-group membership when policy effects follow
Broadening from one user to a group

effects: Change user-driven dynamic membership and effective policies
external_effects: Sign-in and sign-out can deliver or remove device configuration and connected-service accounts
destructive_effects: Sign-out or group removal can revoke required account, mail, VPN, application, or restriction state
concurrency_cautions: External identity synchronization may change user-group membership
Account for all simultaneous device sessions
Detect sign-in state changes during verification

preconditions: Resolve exact user or user group and authoritative membership source
Enumerate all current devices and sessions
Confirm published policies and expected sign-in/sign-out behavior
read_back: Read user-group membership, device-user association, dynamic device membership, policy assignment, and policy status
audit: Match user-group, device-group, policy-link, and sign-in-related administrative events where available
functional_checks: Use one approved test identity to verify sign-in activation and sign-out deactivation on a pilot device
stop_conditions: Policies remain active after intended sign-out or disappear during sign-in

requirements: Capture prior filter tree, user-group membership, device associations, and policy links
Preserve a device baseline independent of user sign-in
limitations: Sign-in state and external group synchronization can re-trigger membership
Removed account data or application state may require manual recovery

contract_checks: Inspect user and user-group filter discriminators and stable identifiers
Locate current device-user association and computed membership reads
Separate user-group membership changes from device-group filter changes

evidence.claim: Relution documents dynamic user and user-group filters, sign-in-driven membership and policy activation, sign-out deactivation, requirements, and simultaneous multi-device matching.

records.name: Event-based device-group actions
records.summary: Device-group membership can trigger an action when a device enters, leaves, or does either, and the action can run immediately or after a delay; action types include deletion, device commands, notifications, renaming, policy refresh, and webhooks.
capabilities: Trigger on group entry
Trigger on group exit
Trigger on both entry and exit
Dispatch immediately or after a configured delay
Delete a device from Relution administration
Run platform-supported device actions such as lost mode, reboot, lock, passcode reset, Return to Service, or wipe
Send notifications, change device names, refresh device policy, or call a webhook
prerequisites: Resolve exact group, trigger direction, delay, action type, payload, and platform applicability
Freeze expected membership transition set
Classify each action's direct and downstream effect
Confirm whether the action modifies a field used by its own or a reachable dynamic filter
Obtain action-specific immediate approval for destructive or externally visible effects

scope.organization_behavior: The rule is attached to one organization device group, but its device actions and webhooks can affect managed endpoints and external services.

reasons: An immediate trigger can execute as soon as membership changes
Entry and exit can both fire
Delete device, wipe, Return to Service, local-user deletion, lock, and passcode reset are destructive or disruptive
An action that changes a filter input can oscillate membership and retrigger
risk.blast_radius: Every device entering or leaving the group during the rule's active lifetime and every external webhook recipient.

required_for: Creating, enabling, changing, duplicating, or deleting an event rule
Any immediate dispatch
Delete, wipe, reset, lock, lost-mode, user deletion, script, application, webhook, notification, rename, or policy-refresh effect

effects: Create or change event-triggered group automation
Dispatch an action on entry, exit, or both
external_effects: Sends commands to devices, messages to users, or requests to webhooks
destructive_effects: Device deletion is documented as irreversible
Wipe and Return to Service reset devices
Local-user deletion and passcode changes can remove access or data
concurrency_cautions: Do not activate before the group and transition set are stable
Reject feedback loops through filter fields
Do not retry unknown action outcomes without target-proven idempotency

preconditions: Trigger, delay, action, target set, platform support, approval, and rollback are explicit
No self-triggering filter feedback path exists
A pilot transition can be generated safely
read_back: Read the saved rule and group membership
Read per-device action status and resulting device state
Read webhook outcome without exposing credentials
audit: Match rule mutation, membership transition, action creation, per-device outcome, and external-effect time
functional_checks: Exercise one non-destructive pilot transition before any higher-risk action
For destructive actions, use only the explicitly approved disposable target
stop_conditions: Platform applicability is mixed or unknown
An unapproved device or external recipient is affected

requirements: Capture prior rule and group state
Disable or detach the trigger before membership repair when separately authorized
Define action-specific compensation
limitations: Device deletion, wipe, Return to Service, local-user deletion, and delivered external messages cannot be undone faithfully
Delayed actions may already be queued

contract_checks: Inspect trigger direction, delay, enabled state, and action discriminator schemas
Confirm platform-specific action applicability and destructive options
Locate queued, per-device, terminal, and partial-failure status operations

evidence.claim: Relution documents entry, exit, or both event triggers; immediate or delayed dispatch; group-action types; and destructive device actions including irreversible device deletion and device reset behavior.

records.name: CRON-scheduled device-group actions
records.summary: A device group can run actions on a CRON-like schedule using minute, hour, day-of-month, month, and day-of-week fields with documented wildcard, list, range, and step operators.
capabilities: Schedule actions by minute values from 0 through 59
Schedule actions by hour values from 0 through 23
Schedule actions by day-of-month values from 1 through 31
Schedule actions by month values from 1 through 12 or JAN through DEC
Schedule actions by day-of-week values from 0 through 6, where 0 is Sunday
Use asterisk for every value, comma for lists, hyphen for ranges, and slash for step intervals
Require at least one selected time value
Run the supported group action types on each matching occurrence
prerequisites: Resolve exact schedule representation, timezone, activation behavior, group, action, and platform applicability from the target contract and runtime
Calculate the next bounded execution times
Freeze expected membership at each canary execution
Confirm repeated execution is safe and idempotent or explicitly intended
Obtain action-specific approval

scope.organization_behavior: The schedule belongs to an organization device group and repeatedly affects whoever is a member when each occurrence is evaluated.

reasons: A schedule repeats actions without a new human decision
A wildcard or malformed assumption can run far more often than intended
Membership can change between occurrences
Destructive actions become repeatedly hazardous
risk.blast_radius: Every group member at every scheduled occurrence and every external service called by the action.

required_for: Creating, enabling, changing, duplicating, or deleting a schedule
Any repeated or destructive action
Wildcard, range, or step expressions
Changing the target group while a schedule is active

effects: Create or change recurring group-action execution
external_effects: Repeatedly sends device commands, notifications, or webhook requests
destructive_effects: Repeated delete, wipe, reset, lock, passcode, user-deletion, script, or application actions can compound damage
concurrency_cautions: Do not assume timezone or CRON dialect
Prevent overlapping runs
Do not replay unknown outcomes
Re-evaluate dynamic membership before each approved canary

preconditions: Schedule fields, timezone, next occurrences, action, membership semantics, and overlap behavior are explicit
One non-destructive canary occurrence is planned
read_back: Read saved schedule, enabled state, next run if exposed, group membership, and per-run/per-device results
audit: Match schedule mutation and each action execution with actor or scheduler identity, group, device, and time
functional_checks: Observe one bounded non-destructive occurrence and ensure it runs exactly once at the expected time

requirements: Capture prior schedule, enabled state, and action
Disable future occurrences before repairing effects when separately authorized
Prepare per-action compensation
limitations: Already executed destructive actions and external requests cannot be recalled
In-flight or queued occurrences may require separate cancellation

contract_checks: Confirm timezone and exact schedule schema instead of assuming standard CRON text
Inspect enablement, overlap, cancellation, and next-run behavior
Locate per-run and per-device status with terminal and partial-failure states

evidence.claim: Relution documents CRON-scheduled device-group actions, allowed time fields and ranges, required time selection, and wildcard, list, range, and step operators.

records.name: User groups, permission sets, and additive effective access
records.summary: Relution supports precise custom permission sets and default permission templates; all permissions assigned to a user are additive, so effective access is the union of direct and group/role-derived assignments rather than a deny-overrides model.
capabilities: Use organization default permission templates that are generated and cannot be modified
Create custom permission sets
Grant fine-grained Read, Create, Update, and Delete capabilities where exposed
Grant individual device-action permissions
Assign permissions to user accounts and groups or roles where supported
Combine every permission assigned to a user additively
Enable MFA requirements through permissions
Use user-group membership as a dynamic device-group policy filter
prerequisites: Resolve exact user, user-group, permission, role, and organization IDs
Enumerate direct, group-derived, global, default, and externally synchronized assignments
Retain a tested recovery administrator
Confirm authoritative membership source and synchronization direction
Calculate effective access before and after the proposed change

scope.organization_behavior: Permission templates and assignments are evaluated in their organization or global scope; externally synchronized membership may overwrite local changes according to target-specific authority rules.

reasons: Additive permissions can grant more access than any single assignment suggests
Removing one assignment may leave equivalent access through another
Privilege changes can lock out administrators or authorize destructive device actions
User-group changes can also alter user-based policy targeting
risk.blast_radius: One user, all members of a security group, an organization, or global administration depending on the assignment scope.

required_for: Creating, updating, deleting, or assigning a permission set or role
Adding or removing security-group membership
MFA requirement changes
Granting device-action or cross-organization privileges

external_effects: May immediately alter portal and API access and may be overwritten by an external identity source
destructive_effects: Can remove the last administrator path or grant authority for destructive operations
concurrency_cautions: Re-read all additive assignments immediately before mutation
Do not update identity-provider mappings and local permissions in the same unverified step
Expect cached sessions or tokens to refresh on target-defined timing

preconditions: Complete before/after effective-permission matrix exists
Recovery administrator is tested
External source of authority and sync schedule are known
User-based policy dependencies are enumerated
read_back: Read user and group memberships, permission and role assignments, effective permissions, MFA requirement, and downstream dynamic-group membership
audit: Match permission, role, group-membership, MFA, and synchronization events
functional_checks: Test allowed and denied behavior with one approved non-critical identity while retaining recovery access

requirements: Capture complete direct and inherited assignments and membership
Keep recovery administrator session available
Prepare external-directory correction if it is authoritative
limitations: Cached sessions or tokens may retain old access until target-defined refresh
Externally synchronized membership may not be recoverable through a local-only change

contract_checks: Separate permission definitions, role definitions, assignments, and group membership
Locate an effective-permission read or compute the additive union from complete assignments
Identify default immutable templates, global scope, and external synchronization behavior

evidence.claim: Relution documents immutable default permission templates, custom fine-grained permissions, typical Read/Create/Update/Delete options, individual device-action permissions, MFA enablement, and additive effective permissions.
Relution documents using user-group membership to target policies through dynamic device groups.
